title: Net worth change and legal settlements paid to Trump
summary: Forbes and Bloomberg both estimate Donald Trump's fortune at several billion dollars, but neither shows a steady rise. Forbes had him at $4.3B in the 2024 Forbes 400, a record $7.3B in Sept 2025, $6.5B in March 2026 and about $7.0B in Sept 2026, which Forbes says is about $2.7B more than when he won the 2024 election. Bloomberg had the family at $7.7B (Sept 2025), $6.8B (Jan 2026) and $7.8B (June 2026, after adding a stablecoin stake). Forbes attributes most of the gain to crypto and overseas licensing, not stock. Most of the fortune is illiquid or paper value: real estate and golf, a Trump Media stake and crypto. Five companies settled his suits for about $90.5M in headline terms (ABC $15M plus $1M fees, Meta $25M, X about $10M, Paramount $16M, YouTube $24.5M). Trump's 2025 OGE disclosure, read in full here, lists $86.5M of settlements: $56.5M of 'net proceeds' paid to his library foundation (ABC $16M, Paramount $16M, Meta $24.5M), $22M from YouTube paid to the Trust for the National Mall for the White House ballroom, and $8M from X with no note that it went anywhere else. The X money is therefore reported as Trump's own settlement income; lawmakers have asked whether it later reached the foundation, and no answer was found. ABC's own letter shows its money was still in escrow in March 2026. Separately, the roughly $230M Trump claimed from the Justice Department was withdrawn in a May 2026 IRS settlement that paid him nothing; a judge later found that suit collusive, and the appeal is pending.

sub_claims.statement: Forbes estimates of Donald Trump's net worth from late 2024 to Nov 2026.
sub_claims.finding: Forbes 400 (data as of 1 Sept 2024, published Oct 2024): $4.3B, No. 319. Forbes 400 (Sept 2025): $7.3B, a record, up $3B in a year; No. 201. Forbes valued crypto plus cash at about $2.4B, including about $709M in meme-coin holdings, and the Trump Media stake at about $2B (search excerpts; the article is paywalled). Forbes World's Billionaires (10 Mar 2026): $6.5B, up $1.4B in a year (implying about $5.1B in the 2025 list); No. 645. Crypto tokens were valued at about $570M, the remaining 38% stake in World Liberty Financial at about $240M, and Trump Media at $1.2B (down from $2.6B) (search excerpts and secondary summaries). Forbes 400 (15 Sept 2026): about $7.0B, down $300M; fell to No. 245, on lower prices for the $TRUMP meme coin and Trump Media shares. Forbes's own breakdown (read in full in the Forbes Australia republication of 21 Sept 2026) says he is 'an estimated $2.7 billion richer than when he won the 2024 election', and lists: cryptocurrency and liquid assets $2.4B (liquid assets $1.9B, meme-coin tokens $183M, World Liberty tokens $78M, stablecoin business $233M); golf clubs and resorts $1.8B; real estate investments $1.1B; Trump Media $1B; other assets $700M (licensing and management business $655M); and additional liabilities of about $140M, including legal liabilities of about $94M (the Carroll judgments) and a pledged asset line of about $50M. Secondary sites give a Forbes real-time figure of about $6.8B on 15 Oct 2026; that is single-source. Forbes's method values each asset and subtracts estimated debts; it treated the voiding of the NY civil-fraud penalty as the removal of a large liability.

sub_claims.statement: Bloomberg Billionaires Index estimates of Trump's and his family's wealth.
sub_claims.finding: Bloomberg put Trump at about $6.6B in late Oct 2024 and $6.49B on election day 2024, when Trump Media shares were swinging. A Wikipedia mirror cites $7.08B in Jan 2025, which is single-source. In July 2025 Bloomberg reported that crypto had added at least $620M. On 7 Sept 2025 it reported $1.3B of crypto wealth added in weeks, taking the family to $7.7B. After the crypto slide, a secondary report citing Bloomberg put the family at about $6.6B, below Bloomberg's top-500 cutoff. In a 20 Jan 2026 feature (read in full in Bloomberg Línea's Spanish edition), Bloomberg put the family at $6.8B, roughly flat on the year: crypto added about $1.4B, or about a fifth of the fortune, while Trump Media fell about 66%. Bloomberg excludes locked WLFI founder tokens, worth about $3.8B at the time. On 12 May 2026 it added $660M after finding previously undisclosed WLFI token sales, putting family token-sale proceeds at about $1.55B. On 6 June 2026 (Bloomberg story read in full via the Spokesman-Review) it began counting a $630M stake in WLF's stablecoin business, valued at about $1.7B in all, taking World Liberty holdings to $2.6B, the family's largest asset, and 'the Trumps' total fortune' to $7.8B. No Bloomberg figure later than June 2026 was found. Bloomberg's figures cover the family rather than Trump alone, so they are not directly comparable with Forbes's figures for Trump.

sub_claims.statement: Most of the gain came from crypto and licensing, not stock, and much of the fortune is paper value.
sub_claims.finding: Forbes editor Dan Alexander said almost none of the $3B gain from fall 2024 to fall 2025 came from stock; crypto ventures and overseas licensing were the main drivers. PolitiFact rated Trump's '60 Minutes' remark crediting stocks Mostly False (9 Nov 2026), citing Alexander's estimate that stock was about 10% of his roughly $415M of liquid assets in fall 2024. Asked about the gain, Trump said 'you should've had stock' and that he devotes almost no time to his net worth. On liquidity, Forbes's crypto-plus-cash figure was about $2.4B in Sept 2025 (about a third of $7.3B) and again $2.4B in Sept 2026 (about a third of $7.0B, with $1.9B of it liquid assets). A secondary summary of the March 2026 list gives 'cryptocurrencies and liquid assets' of $2.1B, about a third of $6.5B; that is single-source. The rest is real estate, golf, licensing businesses and a Trump Media stake that is listed but held in trust and large relative to trading volume. Crypto token values are themselves volatile and partly locked; Bloomberg excludes locked tokens altogether. The ratio is our own arithmetic. A secondary figure of '$8.4B assets, $1.1B liabilities' attributed to Forbes March 2026 nets to $7.3B, the Sept 2025 total, so it appears misattributed and is unverified.

sub_claims.statement: Liabilities: the New York civil fraud judgment and the E. Jean Carroll judgments.
sub_claims.finding: Civil fraud: on 21 Aug 2025 the Appellate Division voided the roughly $464M disgorgement (over $500M with interest) as an excessive fine but upheld the fraud liability finding. Trump asked the NY Court of Appeals to reverse the liability finding (119-page brief, April 2026), and Attorney General Letitia James cross-appealed to restore the penalty (June 2026). No decision had been found as of Sept-Nov 2026. Carroll: the Supreme Court declined to review the $5M verdict in June 2026; a judge ordered about $5.8M (with interest) paid, and Carroll collected it in July 2026. Trump also asked the Court to reconsider that denial (search excerpt; no ruling found). The $83.3M defamation award was upheld by the Second Circuit and is held in a court-controlled account. Trump and the DOJ petitioned the Supreme Court on 28 July 2026, Carroll's brief in opposition was filed on 30 Oct 2026, and no ruling had been found by mid-Nov 2026. Forbes's Sept 2026 tally carries legal liabilities of about $94M for these judgments.

sub_claims.statement: ABC/Disney paid $15M plus $1M in fees to settle Trump's defamation suit (Dec 2024), directed to his presidential library.
sub_claims.finding: The settlement was signed 13-14 Dec 2024 over George Stephanopoulos's on-air statement. Terms: $15M to a 'presidential foundation and museum', $1M in fees, and an editor's note. ABC's 23 Mar 2026 letter to Warren, Blumenthal and Stansbury (read in full) says Disney wired the money on 19 Dec 2024 to the Brito Law PLLC trust account, the escrow set up by Trump's counsel; that release required written notice that the recipient's 501(c)(3) status had been recognized; that Trump's counsel gave that notice for the Donald J. Trump Presidential Library Foundation on 19 Mar 2026; and that ABC was reviewing it and expected to authorize release. ABC also said it would not treat the payment as a charitable contribution on its tax returns. The money was therefore still in escrow in late March 2026. Trump's 2025 OGE disclosure (calendar 2025, read in full) nonetheless lists the ABC settlement at $16M with 'net proceeds paid to The Donald J. Trump Presidential Library Foundation, Inc.'. Neither the $1M difference from the $15M headline nor the timing is explained; the lawmakers asked the foundation about the $16M figure on 15 Jul 2026. Pending matters reported later include an FCC DEI probe (from Mar 2025) and early station-licence renewal filings (2026); see C33.

sub_claims.statement: Meta paid $25M (Jan 2025) to settle Trump's account-suspension suit, mostly for the library.
sub_claims.finding: The settlement was reported 29 Jan 2025. Press reports said about $22M was earmarked for the library and the rest covered legal fees and co-plaintiffs, and Meta told lawmakers that $22M was intended for the library. Trump's 2025 disclosure (read in full) lists the Meta settlement at $24.5M with 'net proceeds paid to' the library foundation. That is more than the $22M Meta designated, and the gap is unexplained in what we found. Pending at the time and later: the FTC's Instagram/WhatsApp monopoly case, which Meta won at trial in Nov 2025 and the FTC is appealing (C33). Meta also gave $1M to the inaugural fund.

sub_claims.statement: X paid about $10M (Feb 2025) to settle Trump's account-suspension suit.
sub_claims.finding: The WSJ reported about $10M (Feb 2025), NBC confirmed it through a source, and Trump lawyer John Kelly confirmed a settlement without giving terms. No court filing with the amount was found. Trump's 2025 OGE disclosure (read in full) lists 'Donald J. Trump, et al. v Twitter, Inc and Jack Dorsey; Source: X Corp.' as $8,000,000 of settlement income in Part 2. Unlike the ABC, CBS and Meta lines, it carries no note that proceeds were paid to the library foundation, and unlike the YouTube line no note that they went to another entity. The lawmakers' 15 Jul 2026 letter reads it the same way: the $8M was 'paid to the President by X', public reports said it was to go to the library, and 'the disclosures do not clarify if this money went to the Foundation'; they asked the foundation to say whether it received the money and why the figure is $8M rather than $10M. So X's payment is the only settlement in this group that the disclosure reports as Trump's own income without a pass-through; whether he kept it or later gave it to the foundation is not documented. Elon Musk was then leading DOGE and was a top 2024 donor; that is context, not a link.

sub_claims.statement: Paramount paid $16M (July 2025) to settle the '60 Minutes' suit, directed to the library.
sub_claims.finding: Announced 1-2 Jul 2025. Paramount said the $16M includes plaintiffs' fees and costs, that the remainder goes to the future library, that Trump receives nothing directly or indirectly, that there is no apology, and that 60 Minutes will release transcripts of candidate interviews. Paramount denied Trump's claim of about $20M in additional PSAs. Pending at the time: FCC review of the Skydance merger, approved 24 Jul 2025 (C33). Paramount and FCC Chair Carr said the two were unrelated, while Sen. Wyden called it a bribe. Trump's 2025 disclosure (read in full) lists the CBS settlement at $16M with 'net proceeds paid to' the library foundation. Paramount told lawmakers its involvement ended with the payment.

sub_claims.statement: YouTube/Alphabet paid $24.5M (Sept 2025), with $22M directed to the White House ballroom.
sub_claims.finding: Court filing of 29 Sep 2025 (N.D. Cal., a week before a hearing before Judge Gonzalez Rogers): $22M on Trump's behalf to the Trust for the National Mall 'to support the construction of the White House State Ballroom'; $2.5M to co-plaintiffs including the American Conservative Union and Naomi Wolf; no admission of liability. The Trust has said it keeps a 2-2.5% management allocation from each donation. Its posted filings show more than $320M received in 2025. Trump's 2025 disclosure (read in full) lists $22M from Alphabet with 'proceeds paid to The Trust for the National Mall'; no statement from the Trust itself confirming receipt was found. Pending at the time: DOJ's search and ad-tech antitrust remedies against Google (C33).

sub_claims.statement: Settlement money directed to the library foundation is accounted for.
sub_claims.finding: Trump's disclosure (received by OGE 29 Jun 2026 and released 30 Jun 2026; read in full) lists $56.5M of 'net proceeds' paid to the foundation: Meta $24.5M, ABC $16M and CBS/Paramount $16M. The lawmakers' 15 Jul 2026 letter (read in full) compares this with the foundation's 10 Oct 2025 Florida solicitation filing, which reports $50M of revenue and about $7M of spending ($400,000 officer compensation, $490,000 legal fees, $130,000 conferences, $15,000 travel, $50,000 insurance and about $6M listed as 'other'). They allege that at least $6.5M and as much as $14.5M is unaccounted for, rising to $13.5M-$21.5M 'missing or spent with no clear explanation' if the X money is counted, and asked for answers by 29 Jul 2026. A Substack analysis argues the Florida figure was a budget, not actual revenue. Our own observation, which no source makes: ABC's letter shows its $15M was still in escrow in March 2026, so the $50M reported in October 2025 could not have included ABC's money, which bears on the lawmakers' arithmetic. The foundation told CBS it expected to file fiscal-2025 disclosures by 15 Nov 2026; no filing was found yet, and no public answer to the letter was found. Money paid to a foundation is not personal income to Trump, although he and his family control the foundation (Eric Trump is its president).

sub_claims.statement: Trump sought about $230M from the Justice Department through administrative claims.
sub_claims.finding: Per the NYT (Oct 2025), Trump filed two Federal Tort Claims Act administrative claims in 2023-24, over the Russia investigation and the 2022 Mar-a-Lago search, together seeking about $230M. Trump said on 21 Oct 2025 he 'could be' seeking it: 'I'm not looking for money. I'd give it to charity or something' (CNN, read in full); DOJ declined comment. On 18 May 2026, Trump, his sons and the Trump Organization settled their $10B suit against the IRS over the leak of his tax returns. DOJ said they would receive a formal apology but 'no monetary payment or damages of any kind', and that Trump's team agreed to drop the administrative claims (CBS News, read in full). DOJ instead created a $1.776B 'anti-weaponization fund' from the Judgment Fund for others, for which Trump was not eligible. Reporting also says the deal gave audit protections; that is single-source. In July 2026, Judge Kathleen Williams found the suit collusive and brought in bad faith, voided reliance on the settlement and sanctioned Trump's counsel, including Alejandro Brito. Acting AG Blanche told Congress the fund was 'not moving forward, period'. On about 29 Sept 2026 an 11th Circuit panel declined to stay the sanctions, saying Trump and his lawyers offered no evidence that the suit and settlement were not collusive; the underlying appeal is pending. Net result: no payment to Trump is documented.

sub_claims.statement: Other settlements or pending suits; law-firm pledges (kept separate).
sub_claims.finding: We found no settlement payment to Trump in 2026. Pending or failed suits: the WSJ/Dow Jones $10B suit was dismissed with prejudice on 31 Oct 2026 (Trump says he will press on). The BBC $10B suit's defamation claim was allowed to proceed on about 11 Nov 2026. The NYT $15B suit is pending, and the Des Moines Register/Selzer suit was being contested. JPMorgan ($5B, filed Jan 2026) and Capital One are fighting debanking suits rather than settling. Law firms' pro bono pledges (nine firms, about $940M per Bloomberg Law, April 2025) are commitments of free legal services to causes the administration favours. They are not payments to Trump and are not counted in the ledger.

corrections: Claimed (C33): Meta paid about $22M of $25M to the library. The record shows: Trump's 2025 OGE disclosure lists $24.5M of net proceeds paid to the library foundation from the Meta settlement; Meta told lawmakers $22M was designated. The difference is unexplained. (Applied to C33 on 16 Nov 2026.)

Claimed (C33): ABC paid $15M to the library. The record shows: the disclosure lists the ABC settlement at $16M with net proceeds paid to the foundation, while ABC's own March 2026 letter says the $15M was still in escrow pending release. The $1M difference and the timing are unexplained. (Applied to C33.)

Claimed (C33): no payment went to Trump personally. The record shows: the disclosure reports $8M from X as Trump's own settlement income with no note that it went to the foundation; whether he kept it is not documented. The statement holds for ABC, Meta, Paramount and YouTube. (Applied to C33.)
Claimed (C33): X paid about $10M. The record shows: the press figure is unchanged, but the disclosure lists $8M; how the other roughly $2M was split (fees, other parties) is unknown.

Claimed (C55): Bloomberg put the family at about $6.7B after the crypto slide. The record shows: Bloomberg's 20 Jan 2026 feature gives $6.8B and a secondary report citing Bloomberg gives about $6.6B; C55 also predates Bloomberg's 6 June 2026 figure of $7.8B and the Forbes 400 figure of about $7.0B (15 Sept 2026).

Claimed in secondary coverage: Forbes's March 2026 list shows $8.4B of assets and $1.1B of liabilities. The record shows: those numbers net to $7.3B, the Sept 2025 total, not $6.5B, so the attribution appears wrong; treated as unverified.

Claimed in some coverage: Forbes put Trump at about $6.3B on election day 2024. The record shows: Forbes's 2024 Forbes 400 figure was $4.3B (as of 1 Sept 2024), and Forbes's Sept 2026 article says he is about $2.7B richer than when he won the election at about $7.0B, implying about $4.3B. The $6.3B figure matches Bloomberg-range numbers; treated as unverified for Forbes.

Claimed in this check's first draft: some coverage gives a 2024 Forbes 400 figure of $3.9B, and the Forbes component split for Sept 2026 was unverified. The record shows: Forbes's own Oct 2024 article gives $4.3B (No. 319), and Forbes's own Sept 2026 breakdown confirms meme coin $183M, World Liberty tokens $78M, stablecoin business $233M and licensing and management $655M.

Claimed in this check's first draft: YouTube's $24.5M is the amount directed to the Trust for the National Mall (ledger range $22M-$24.5M). The record shows: only $22M went to the Trust; $2.5M went to co-plaintiffs.
denials_and_context: Trump, on '60 Minutes' (Nov 2026), credited the stock market for his gains, said he devotes almost no time to his net worth and that he takes no salary. Forbes's Dan Alexander called this 'nonsense', and PolitiFact rated it Mostly False.

Net-worth figures are outside estimates, not disclosures. Forbes and Bloomberg differ in scope (Trump alone vs family), in how they treat locked tokens (Bloomberg excludes them) and in valuation dates. Swings mostly track Trump Media shares and crypto prices.

Paramount and FCC Chair Carr said the settlement was unrelated to the merger review. Paramount said Trump receives nothing directly or indirectly and denied the PSA claim. ABC said it will not deduct the payment. Meta and Paramount told lawmakers they paid as their agreements required. YouTube's filing admits no liability.

The regulatory matters listed for each company are reported context. No document links any settlement to any regulatory outcome, and several payers later faced adverse federal action (FTC v. Meta appeal, DOJ v. Google appeals, FCC probes of ABC).
The library foundation and Eric Trump had not answered the lawmakers' questions publicly in the sources found; the White House has generally referred library questions to the foundation.

Money directed to the library foundation or the ballroom trust is not personal income to Trump, but he and his family control the foundation and he directs the ballroom project. The lawmakers' 'missing money' figures are allegations; the foundation had not answered publicly as of the sources found.

The IRS settlement and the $230M claims: DOJ says it paid Trump nothing. A federal judge found the suit collusive; Trump's side is appealing. Democratic lawmakers argued any payment would raise domestic-emoluments issues.

Source limits: the original research read every source as a search excerpt. In the November 2026 second review, Trump's 2025 OGE Form 278e (settlement lines), the lawmakers' 15 Jul 2026 letter, ABC's 23 Mar 2026 letter, Forbes's Oct 2024 and Sept 2026 Trump profiles (Forbes Australia republications), Bloomberg's Jan and June 2026 figures (syndicated copies), and the PolitiFact, CNN, CBS, PBS, NPR, NBC New York and Raw Story items were read in full. The Forbes Sept 2025 and March 2026 articles are paywalled and remain search excerpts.

checked: Settlement amounts, dates and destinations against Trump's 2025 OGE Form 278e line 431, especially that X paid $8M to Trump personally
ABC's escrow and release timeline against ABC's 23 Mar 2026 letter; the lawmakers' 15 Jul 2026 letter and its 'missing money' figures

Status of the NY civil-fraud appeal, the Carroll judgments, and the withdrawal of the roughly $230M claims in the IRS settlement
changes: Read the OGE 278e in full: $86.5M of settlements (X $8M; ABC $16M, CBS $16M and Meta $24.5M with 'net proceeds paid to' the foundation; YouTube $22M 'paid to' the Trust for the National Mall). $56.5M to the foundation and $78.5M to the foundation or the Trust reconcile with the table.

Softened 'X paid $8M to Trump personally': the disclosure reports it as his settlement income with no pass-through note, and the lawmakers say the same, but whether he kept it or later passed it to the foundation is not documented. Rewrote sub-claim 7, the summary, the relationship label and ledger row C100-12.

ABC: ABC's letter, read in full, shows the money was still in Brito Law's escrow on 23 Mar 2026, with notice of the foundation's 501(c)(3) status given only on 19 Mar 2026. Corrected the earlier statement that release followed the Oct 2025 IRS recognition; the 2025 disclosure's 'net proceeds paid' wording and the $16M figure remain unexplained. Added, as our own observation, that ABC's money could not be in the foundation's Oct 2025 revenue.

Forbes: confirmed the 2024 Forbes 400 figure of $4.3B (No. 319, as of 1 Sept 2024) and removed the unsupported $3.9B; the '$2.7B richer since the election' is Forbes's own statement, not PolitiFact's. The Sept 2026 component split previously marked unverified is confirmed by Forbes's own breakdown. The '$8.4B assets / $1.1B liabilities' and 'Forbes $6.3B on election day' figures remain unverified.
Bloomberg: confirmed $6.8B (20 Jan 2026) and $7.8B (6 June 2026) from syndicated full texts; replaced the Daily Herald link, which no longer serves the story, with the Spokesman-Review copy.

Ledger: YouTube row C100-14 reduced from $22M-$24.5M to $22M (the $2.5M went to co-plaintiffs, not the Trust); Meta row C100-11 high end set to the disclosed $24.5M; Forbes rows C100-01 and C100-09 tightened; added overlap notes with C96-29, which lists the same $86.5M disclosure line.

Liabilities and claims: the civil-fraud appeal is still undecided as far as we found; Carroll collected about $5.8M on the $5M verdict in July 2026 and her opposition brief on the $83.3M petition was filed 30 Oct 2026; DOJ's statement that the IRS deal paid Trump nothing and that his team dropped the $230M claims is confirmed; the 11th Circuit's denial of a stay (about 29 Sept 2026) is added.
